constitutive_assumptions: NinjaFlex material modeled using the Yeoh hyperelastic model
Frictionless contact model between the actuator and the obstacle in FE simulations
Omission of internal air channels from the FE simulation mesh with minimal displacement error (reported as 2.598% in free bending and 0.996% in hindered bending) to reduce computational load
Connecting block treated as an equivalent beam structure whose lateral bending and twisting resistance improves with a wider and shorter cross-section
control_variables: Actuation air pressure fixed at 100 kPa across simulations and physical experiments
External dimensions of each SPBA unit fixed at 30 mm width x 30 mm height x 10 mm length
Bottom layer thickness fixed at 5 mm
Auxiliary denominator parameter epsilon set to 1 mm in out-of-plane stiffness formulation
Target unobstructed bending angle constraint set to 1.5 rad for the 4-unit SPBA optimization
Finger assembly angle fixed at 60 degrees from the central axis on the 4-finger gripper frame
Drop weight mass fixed at 0.5 kg in dynamic experiments
dependent_variables: Out-of-plane displacement (U) of the actuator tip from the pure bending plane
Out-of-plane deformation force (F) generated normal to the bending plane
Unobstructed bending angle (theta) under collision-free actuation
Escape displacement of grasped and caged spheres under quasi-static pulling loads
Grasping and caging retention stability under dynamic impact momentum

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Out-of-plane deformation under asymmetric loading causes unexpected buckling and twisting, reducing grasping stability in soft grippers.
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: Background and problem motivation supported by prior literature

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Decoupling FEA simulation from the optimization loop by training a differentiable RBF neural network metamodel prevents non-convergence caused by nonlinear FEA instability.
Sensitivity analysis demonstrated that chamber fillet radii have negligible impact on bending and twisting behavior, permitting model reduction to four key parameters: HC, LA, TA, and WB.

Parametric optimization of the 4-unit SPBA increased out-of-plane stiffness by 88.1% in FE simulations and by 75.0% in physical experiments while matching the required unobstructed bending angle under 100 kPa.

During quasi-static sphere extraction tests, peak out-of-plane displacements near the fingertips of unoptimized grippers were on average 1.59 times (caging) and 1.82 times (grasping) larger than those of the optimized gripper.

In dynamic impact tests with momentum of 0.62 kg m/s for caging and 0.85 kg m/s for grasping, the optimized gripper retained the objects across all 10 trials, whereas the unoptimized design failed every trial.

experimental_setup: 4-unit SPBA testbench: NinjaFlex 85A 3D-printed actuator, inclined ramp mounted on a KERN EHA1000-1 electronic scale, and vision system measuring out-of-plane displacement and bending angle at 100 kPa
4-finger soft gripper: Four fingers each composed of 7 repeated SPBA units (NinjaFlex) with hemispherical PLA fingertips mounted at 60 degrees from the central axis
Pressure supply and regulation: Jun-Air Model 6-15 Litre air compressor with electronic pressure control module delivering 100 kPa
Motion capture system: Six Vicon Vero v1.3 cameras tracking retroreflective markers placed on the 2nd, 4th, and 6th bellows and pulling string at up to 250 FPS
Quasi-static test: Inextensible string pulling a caged 50 mm sphere or grasped 70 mm sphere slowly out of the gripper
Dynamic impact test: Triggered release mechanism dropping a 0.5 kg mass from heights of 78 mm (caging) and 146 mm (grasping) to apply impact momentum of 0.62 and 0.85 kg m/s
future_work: Investigating material stiffness modification in conjunction with or in place of geometric optimization for actuator designs lacking large geometric variation (e.g., Galloway-type fiber-reinforced actuators)
independent_variables: SPBA geometric design parameters: connecting block height (HC), connecting block length / gap dimension (LA), shell thickness (TA), and connecting block width (WB)
Gripper design version: initial unoptimized baseline vs. data-driven optimized design
Loading mode and magnitude: quasi-static pull displacement (up to 40 mm) vs. dynamic impact momentum (0.62 and 0.85 kg m/s from 0.5 kg mass dropped from 78 mm and 146 mm)
Object diameter and grasping mode: 50 mm diameter sphere for caging vs. 70 mm diameter sphere for grasping
limitations_inferred: The objective function relies on interaction with an idealized rigid ramp, which may not capture the contact mechanics of irregular, compliant, or high-friction objects
Offline dataset generation for the RBF surrogate requires running thousands of nonlinear FEA simulations (4,480 training points), incurring substantial upfront computational cost
Simulation assumed frictionless contact, which omits tangential shear traction present in real physical grasping interactions
Dynamic evaluations were restricted to spherical objects and vertical drop impacts, leaving torsional disturbances and cyclic fatigue uncharacterized
limitations_stated_by_authors: Sensitivity analysis was evaluated solely at the median values of parameter ranges, which might not capture interactions across all parameter combinations
The framework focuses solely on geometric optimization with fixed material properties, making it inapplicable to actuators without geometric variation where material stiffness modulation is essential
Simplifying the FE simulation by excluding the air channel introduces minor modeling discrepancy (slightly elevating simulated bending and torsional resistance)
Study demonstrates optimization on a single actuator architecture (fast pneu-net SPBA) under a fixed actuation pressure of 100 kPa
main_results: FE simulation showed an 88.1% improvement in out-of-plane stiffness (from 0.042 N/mm to 0.079 N/mm) for the 4-unit SPBA at 100 kPa while strictly maintaining the 1.5 rad unobstructed bending angle

Physical experiments on the 4-unit SPBA verified a 75.0% increase in out-of-plane stiffness (from 0.040 N/mm to 0.070 N/mm) with virtually identical bending angles (1.498 rad baseline vs. 1.495 rad optimized)

In quasi-static pulling tests, unoptimized 7-unit fingers exhibited maximum out-of-plane displacements averaging 1.59x higher (caging a 50 mm sphere) and 1.82x higher (grasping a 70 mm sphere) than optimized fingers

In dynamic impact tests (10 trials each), the optimized gripper successfully resisted impact momenta of 0.62 kg m/s (caged sphere) and 0.85 kg m/s (grasped sphere), whereas the baseline gripper failed in all tests
A dataset of 4,480 training points was identified as the optimal balance between surrogate fitting accuracy and FEA data generation efficiency
modeling_methods: Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in Abaqus/CAE using hexahedral meshes and frictionless contact formulation
Model reduction via 1D parameter sweep sensitivity analysis to reduce an 8-parameter model down to 4 parameters (HC, LA, TA, WB)
Quasi-random sampling of the 4D parameter space using Sobol sequences
Metamodeling with Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural networks utilizing 2D thin-plate spline basis functions to fit continuous proxy functions for U(x), F(x), and theta(x)
Sequential Least-Squares Programming (SLSQP) for constrained gradient-based numerical optimization
performance_metrics: Out-of-plane stiffness (ko = F / (U + epsilon)) in N/mm
Unobstructed bending angle (theta) in radians or degrees
Metamodel fitting error expressed as coefficient of variation (sigma / mu)
Maximum out-of-plane displacement (mm) and displacement ratio between baseline and optimized fingers
Critical impact momentum (kg m/s) resisted without object escape
possible_gap_implications: The data-driven surrogate modeling workflow could be adapted to optimize other soft actuator topologies where direct FEA-in-the-loop numerical optimization suffers from non-convergence
Extending the framework to simultaneously optimize geometry and spatially heterogeneous or variable stiffness materials could further increase payload resistance without compromising compliance
Incorporating diverse obstacle geometries and friction into the surrogate training dataset could lead to grippers optimized for arbitrary unstructured manipulation tasks
paper.research_objective: To establish a data-driven optimization framework that maximizes out-of-plane stiffness in soft grippers (achieving hard-to-twist and easy-to-bend mechanical properties) while preserving a required unobstructed bending angle under pneumatic actuation.
paper.research_problem: High structural and material compliance in soft grippers leads to unwanted out-of-plane lateral bending, twisting, and buckling under asymmetric loads, causing grasping failure; additionally, integrating nonlinear FEA directly into numerical optimization loops frequently fails due to numerical non-convergence.
paper.title: Optimizing Out-of-Plane Stiffness for Soft Grippers
